locator: §4.1, 'When those words occur in the antecedent of a conditional, or when a person says, ‘I wonder if lying is wrong’ they they are typically not being used to express such disapproval'
interpretation: The datum behind Geach's argument: in the antecedent of a conditional the moral sentence is not used to express 'such disapproval', the attitude it expresses free-standing; Geach's first premise is one 'one might accept even if one approves of tormenting cats'. Read as: the antecedent occurrence does not express the attitude the free-standing occurrence expresses. It does not say the antecedent expresses no attitude whatever (Codex P1 on #187). The entry says 'typically', so the reading is stated for the one sentence of Geach's example, not for every moral sentence. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
